newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Mixed day leaves Brussels bourse seeking direction.
newsitem.headline: Mixed day leaves Brussels bourse seeking direction.

text.p: The Brussels stock market ended a mixed Tuesday with no clear direction and traders nervous over the next move.

"Several shares came back from their highs but others had a lot of interest," one trader said. "It is clear that the recent dollar weakness has had no market impact, but a lot will depend on what New York does next."
The Bel-20 blue chip share index ended 0.03 percent higher at 2,242.94 with eight gainers, two unchanged and 10 unchanged. More than three billion francs worth of Belgian shares were traded.
"I am hoping for a correction, otherwise investors will start to dream that there is only one direction, and that is dengerous," one trader said.
Others, however, said the market had a full head of steam and was headed higher no matter what.
Oil major PetroFina was the busiest share of the day by value, climbing one percent to 12,925 francs in a volume of more than 26,000 shares after a positive profit outlook on Monday.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert was the biggest climber in the index, rising 2.5 percent to 6,490 francs.
On the down side, shipper CMB fell 1.2 percent to 2,400 francs after analysts reviewed their attitude to the shares following a meeting with management.
Retailer GIB also suffered, falling 0.6 percent to 1,560 francs due toa combination of negative comments from French analysts and players switching out into subsidiary Quick.
Fellow retailer Colruyt suffered too, dropping 1.9 percent to 14,125 as players took profits.
